land.text: the Zagwe kingdom: Lasta, Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara (the af-01-a hand-over)

predecessors.note: Ethiopian Empire page: Yekuno Amlak 'replaced the Agaw kingdom of the Zagwe' in 1270; Cliopatria keeps the Zagwe row to 1271 and starts this row in 1272.

land.text: the whole empire, annexed by Italy on 9 May 1936 and merged into Italian East Africa on 1 June 1936

successors.note: The Second Italo-Ethiopian War page: Addis Ababa fell 5 May 1936, annexation announced 9 May, Italian East Africa formed 1 June 1936. Sovereignty was restored on 5 May 1941 (Ethiopian Empire page infobox); the restored state is Cliopatria's 'Ethiopia' row (slug ethiopia, from 1942), written by another part of group af-01. Cliopatria's Italian Africa shape for 1936 already contains Ethiopia.

capitals.name: Itinerant royal court (no fixed capital)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: None (1270-1635)'. The dot is placed at the centre of Cliopatria's 1272 shape and is not a city; the court moved between camps.

capitals.name: Gondar
capitals.note: Infobox gives Gondar 1635-1855; the body of the Ethiopian Empire page and the Gondarine page say Gondar was founded 'in 1636 as a permanent capital'. Coordinates are the researcher's (Gondar is in the gazetteer).

capitals.name: Debre Tabor

capitals.note: Infobox: Addis Ababa 1889-1974; the Menelik II page says he moved his capital to Addis Ababa in 1886. The state ends in 1936 here.

correction.text: Yekuno Amlak's realm at its start, taken as Cliopatria's 1272 shape; the page names no extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's first Ethiopian Empire shape starts in 1272, but the page puts Yekuno Amlak's ascension in 1270 ('replaced the Agaw kingdom of the Zagwe'). The page gives no extent for 1270-1271, so the 1272 shape is carried back two years (the zagwe-dynasty row ends 1271). Confidence 1: page silent on the extent.

209,304 km2. The Ethiopian Empire page gives no area before the 1954 figure (1,221,900 km2) and no extent for the first reigns, so the shape stands as the Solomonic kingdom after the Zagwe (Tigray to Shewa highlands).

208,160 km2, almost the same shape as 1272 (the eastern edge moves 0.05 degrees). The page records only the succession of Yagbe'u Seyon in 1285; the Shewa page dates Ifat's conquest of the Sultanate of Shewa to 1285 on the eastern border, which is the likely reason Cliopatria redraws the edge there.

391,551 km2, 1.9 times the 1285 shape. The Amda Seyon page calls the result 'the new empire, several times larger than that of his predecessors' and dates the campaigns 1316 (Damot, Hadiya, Gojjam), 1329 (Semien, Wegera, Tselemt, Tsegede) and 1332 (Ifat, Dawaro, Bale across the Awash). The growth between 1316 and 1332 is carried by the ledger; the shape is the end state, so it holds for 1333-1403. Ifat (Cliopatria's own row) is a vassal inside this reach 1332-1403.

correction.text: the empire plus the former Ifat land after Dawit I's victory of 1403 (Cliopatria's Ifat 1407 shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1404-1414. The Ifat page: 'Ifat's troops were defeated in 1403 on the Harar plateau' and the sultanate ended (infobox disestablished 1403); the Ethiopian Empire page says the sultanate ended when Zeila was captured by Dawit I. Cliopatria keeps Ifat as a separate state until 1414. This keyframe adds Ifat's former land to the empire until the Walashma return in 1415. Confidence 2: the pages say the sultanate ended but not that Ethiopian officials ruled the land.

392,042 km2, the 1333 shape again. The Adal page: 'In 1415, Sabr ad-Din III ... would return to Adal from his exile in Arabia'; the Walashma refounded the sultanate as Adal, so the Ifat land leaves the empire (ledger 1415). The war with Yeshaq I (1415-1429) and Zara Yaqob's Gomit victory of 1445 moved no border the pages name.
392,042 km2, identical to the 1415 shape (same area to the decimal); the page records no change in 1502, so the split of the row at 1502 is Cliopatria's bookkeeping.

381,441 km2, a 3 percent cut from the 1502 shape. The Adal page: Imam Ahmad 'finally decided to embark on a conquest of Abyssinia' in 1529; Shimbra Kure was an Adal victory in March 1529 (Ethiopian-Adal War page). The page dates the occupation of Dawaro and Shewa to 1531 and Bete Amhara and Lasta to 1533, so Cliopatria's net cut here is small and the main loss is drawn in 1534.

126,100 km2: the northern rump. The Ethiopian Empire page: 'by the mid 1530s most of Ethiopia was under Adalite occupation'; the Ethiopian-Adal War page: Ahmad took Aksum and held Tigray 'roughly a year' from 1535, which the ledger carries (Tigray lost 1535, regained 1536).

correction.text: unchanged, for 1540-1543; the pre-war realm is complete from October 1544

keyframe_review.note: The shape (126,789 km2) is right for 1540-1542 and holds through 1543 as the net of the retreat. The Ethiopian-Adal War page: Lebna Dengel died 2 September 1540, the Portuguese landed in February 1541, Ahmad was beheaded on 21 February 1543 and his death 'forced an Adalite retreat from Ethiopia'; his vizier Abbas held Bali, Fatagar and Dawaro until Gelawdewos killed him in October 1544; the infobox result is 'status quo ante bellum'. The ledger carries the recovery (1543 highlands, October 1544 south); from 1544 use the new keyframe ethiopian-empire_1544.

correction.text: the realm as before the invasion: 'status quo ante bellum' plus 'the reconquest of former territories'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1544-1546. The infobox gives 'status quo ante bellum' with 'reconquest of former territories', and Gelawdewos recovered Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya in October 1544, so the pre-war shape (Cliopatria 1502) is the page-backed extent. Cliopatria waits until 1547 to restore the highlands.

correction.text: the pre-war realm, restored in 1543-1544; the extra eastern land of Cliopatria's 1547 shape has no support on the pages opened

keyframe_review.note: 526,425 km2, 134,000 km2 more than the pre-war shape and reaching Djibouti (42.8 E). No page opened gives the empire any gain beyond the 1544 recovery (status quo ante bellum), and Adal still held the Harar plateau and Zeila coast until 1577. The page-backed shape is the pre-war one. The Ethiopian Empire page has no area figure before 1954.

correction.text: the pre-war realm; Massawa and the coast go to the Ottomans in 1557 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 523,787 km2, same objection as 1547. The page adds that from 1557 the Ottomans held Massawa (Habesh Eyalet) and that Sarsa Dengel confined them to 'a narrow coastline strip' in 1589; the Red Sea coast is therefore not Ethiopian in this period (ledger 1557).

correction.text: the pre-war realm, before the Oromo losses dated in the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 523,872 km2. The Oromo page: Sarsa Dengel learned of incursions in Shewa in 1574, 'Wej' was taken after the 1572 rains, 'Shewa and Damot were deserted' (1593); the Ethiopian Empire page: 'much of the Empire's southern territory and vassals were lost' and Bale last paid tribute under Yaqob (1590-1607). Cliopatria draws none of this. The pre-war shape is the base and the ledger removes Wej 1572, Shewa and Damot 1593 and Bale 1607.

minus.text: the Gondarine realm in the northern highlands (Tigray, Gojjam, Begemder, Lasta, Amhara), taken as Cliopatria's 1769 shape

correction.text: the Gondarine realm in the northern highlands (Tigray, Gojjam, Begemder, Lasta, Amhara), taken as Cliopatria's 1769 shape; without the Afar lowlands (Sultanate of Aussa)

keyframe_review.note: 587,414 km2, the largest Cliopatria extent until 1908, in the century when the Oromo took the south and the court settled at Gondar (founded 1636). The Gondarine page gives no extent; the Oromo page has the Wallo and Azebo overrunning Angot and parts of Amhara, Waj, Begemder and Tigre in 1620-1660, and Oromo settled inside Gojjam and Begemder. Cliopatria's own 1769 shape (240,302 km2: Tigray, Amhara and the Eritrean highlands) is the page-consistent extent, so it is used for 1636-1768. Confidence 2: no page measures the Gondarine empire. Afar removed (repair fx-28): the Sultanate of Aussa page has the sultanate allied with Italy ('On 6 December 1889, Aussa signed a treaty with the Italians, agreeing to become a protectorate of Italy') until Welde Giyorgis Aboye 'defeated Sultan Muhammad Hanfare at the battle of Arraddo in January 1896', and only then 'Aussa became a tributary of the Ethiopian Empire' with 'a modicum of autonomy'; the Afar lowlands are therefore the sultanate's own land (drawn by sultanate-of-aussa, under Ethiopian suzerainty from 1896, ledger vassal_start), not part of this shape.

240,302 km2 for 1769-1889, one shape through the Zemene Mesafint, Tewodros II and Yohannes IV. The Zemene Mesafint page: emperors 'reduced to little more than figureheads confined to the capital city of Gondar' from 7 May 1769 (Ras Mikael Sehul deposed Iyoas I) to Tewodros II's coronation on 11 February 1855, with Tigray, Yejju (Wollo), Shewa, Gojjam, Simien and Begemder held by regional lords; the Ethiopian Empire page: Yohannes IV 're-expanded into Eritrea' in 1874-1876. The shape stands as the nominal realm; whether the Eritrean highlands were inside during 1769-1874 is not settled by the pages (see notes). Afar removed (repair fx-28): the Sultanate of Aussa page has the sultanate allied with Italy ('On 6 December 1889, Aussa signed a treaty with the Italians, agreeing to become a protectorate of Italy') until Welde Giyorgis Aboye 'defeated Sultan Muhammad Hanfare at the battle of Arraddo in January 1896', and only then 'Aussa became a tributary of the Ethiopian Empire' with 'a modicum of autonomy'; the Afar lowlands are therefore the sultanate's own land (drawn by sultanate-of-aussa, under Ethiopian suzerainty from 1896, ledger vassal_start), not part of this shape.

correction.text: the empire as it stood, until Addis Ababa fell on 5 May 1936; without the Afar lowlands (Sultanate of Aussa)

Cliopatria's Ethiopian row stops in 1935 and its Italian Africa row draws all of Ethiopia from 1936; the pages put the fall of Addis Ababa at 5 May 1936 and the annexation at 9 May, so the empire is drawn for 1936 with the Italian advance as the ledger's contest. region.text: Yekuno Amlak's kingdom after the Zagwe

ledger.note: 1270: Yekuno Amlak ascends and founds the Solomonic line, replacing the Zagwe. 'replaced the Agaw kingdom of the Zagwe'; infobox 'Ascension of Yekuno Amlak: 1270'. The page names no extent, so the region is Cliopatria's 1272 shape. (The zagwe-dynasty dossier, from the Yekuno Amlak page not opened here, gives 10 August 1270.)

1299: Wedem Arad is at war with Ifat over eastern Shewa. The page: Wedem Arad 'seized the throne' by 1299 and was 'in conflict with the Sultanate of Ifat over eastern Shewa'. The page names no battle.

region.text: the pagan kingdom of Damot, conquered in the 1316/7 campaign

ledger.note: 1316: Amda Seyon conquers Damot. The page: a manuscript note says he 'successfully campaigned against the Pagan Damot'; the campaign is dated 1316/7.

1316: Amda Seyon conquers the Muslim kingdom of Hadiya. The same 1316/7 campaign; the page names the 'Muslim Hadiya Kingdom' and later says Hadiya 'had been fully integrated', supplying troops in 1332.
1316: Amda Seyon takes Gojjam. 'in the same year, the emperor also campaigned against the more northerly province of Gojjam.' Gojjam is placed as a radius round Debre Markos.

1329: Amda Seyon campaigns in the northern provinces. 'In 1329, the Emperor campaigned in the northern provinces of Semien, Wegera, Tselemt, and Tsegede.' The page does not say they were annexed; confidence 1 for a gain.

1332: Ifat is defeated and the eastern Shewa quarrel ends. The page: Hadiya troops joined 'his 1332 campaigns against the Sultanate of Ifat', and Sabr ad-Din 'surrendered himself to Amda Seyon's camp'. Huntingford favoured 1329; the page calls 1332 'the generally accepted year'.

region.text: the sultanate of Ifat, from Zequalla to Zeila

ledger.note: 1332: Ifat becomes a vassal. 'Amda Seyon appointed the governor's brother, Jamal ad-Din I, as his successor in Ifat'; he later deposed Jamal for joining a rebellion and appointed Nasir ad-Din as governor. The Ifat page calls the sultan a 'vassal king under Amde Seyon'. Cliopatria keeps Ifat as its own row, drawn here as a vassal.

region.text: Dawaro, Bale and other Muslim states across the Awash

ledger.note: 1332: Ethiopian rule crosses the Awash. 'extended Ethiopian rule for the first time across the Awash River', gaining 'control of Dawaro, Bale, and other Muslim states'. The page ties this to the Ifat campaign without a separate year.

1403: Ifat's sultanate falls. 'Ifat's troops were defeated in 1403 on the Harar plateau' and Maqrizi has Dawit I pursuing the sultan to Zeila (another source gives Sa'ad ad-Din II's death in 1410). The Ethiopian Empire page: Dawit I invaded Ifat and it ended when Zeila was captured. The vassal relation ends with the state.
1403: Dawit I holds Ifat's land. The pages say the sultanate ended; neither says Ethiopian officials ruled the land until the Walashma returned in 1415, so this is a bridge.

region.text: the former Ifat land, now Adal

ledger.note: 1415: the Walashma return and found Adal. 'In 1415, Sabr ad-Din III, the eldest son of Sa'ad ad-Din II, would return to Adal from his exile in Arabia'; the Ethiopian Empire page: 'Walashma returned in 1415 and established the Adal Sultanate, centred on Harar'. The land is Ifat's former land.

region.text: the land Cliopatria adds to Adal in 1529, the first ground of the war

ledger.note: March 1529: Imam Ahmad's army defeats the Ethiopians at Shimbra Kure. 'at Shimbra Kure in March 1529, where Ahmad's forces met the Christian king's army directly for the first time.' The page does not place Shimbra Kure; the region is the strip Cliopatria adds to Adal's shape in 1529.

1531: Adal occupies Dawaro and Shewa. 'Dawaro and Shewa were occupied in 1531' (Adal page); the Ethiopian-Adal War page: 'the victories that gave the followers of Imam Ahmad the upper hand came in 1531' (Antukyah 23 February, Ayfars 31 March).
1533: Adal occupies Bete Amhara and Lasta. 'Bete Amhara and Lasta in 1533' (Adal page). Lasta is placed as a radius round Lalibela.
1535: Adal seizes Aksum and Tigray. 'marching into Tegray and seizing Aksum' (Ethiopian-Adal War page).
1536: Tigray is recovered. The Adal hold on Tigray lasted 'roughly a year' (Ethiopian-Adal War page); the year is the researcher's count from 1535.

region.text: the highlands evacuated by Adal after Wayna Daga, except Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya

ledger.note: 21 February 1543: Imam Ahmad is killed at Wayna Daga and Adal leaves the highlands. 'the wounded Imam was beheaded on 21 February 1543 by an Ethiopian cavalry commander'; his death 'forced an Adalite retreat from Ethiopia'. Infobox: 'status quo ante bellum'. The page lists no provinces for this step; the region is the land Cliopatria gives Adal in 1540 outside its Harar core, less the south that Abbas still held until October 1544.

October 1544: Gelawdewos kills Abbas and recovers the south. 'in October 1544, a year and a half after Ahmad's death, Gelawdewos defeated and killed Abbas', recovering Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya.
October 1544: the war ends in an Ethiopian victory ('Ethiopian-Portuguese victory'). Ahmad died on 21 February 1543; the last dated step is Abbas's death in October 1544.

region.text: Massawa and the coastal strip, Habesh Eyalet

ledger.note: 1557: the Ottomans take the coast. 'From 1557 the Ottomans established Habesh Eyalet after conquering Massawa and seizing Suakin from the Funj Sultanate'; Sarsa Dengel sacked Arqiqo in 1589, 'thus containing them on a narrow coastline strip'.
1572: the Oromo take Wej. 'the Oromo took it after the 1572 rains' (Oromo migrations page). The page places no boundary for Wej.

1593: Shewa and Damot are abandoned to the Oromo. 'Shewa and Damot were deserted' (a passage the page dates to 1593); the Ethiopian Empire page: 'much of the Empire's southern territory and vassals were lost'.
1607: Bale drops out of the tribute list. 'Bale last paid tribute under Yaqob (1590-1607)'; the year is the end of that reign.
1636: Fasilides founds Gondar as the permanent capital. 'Gondar was founded by Emperor Fasilides in 1636 as a permanent capital' (the infobox gives 1635).

7 May 1769: Ras Mikael Sehul deposes Iyoas I and the Era of the Princes begins. 'Ras Mikael Sehul deposed Emperor Iyoas I (7 May 1769)'; the emperors become 'little more than figureheads confined to the capital city of Gondar'. The state keeps its name and colour; the Yejju (Wara Seh) dynasty rules through puppet emperors.
1855: Tewodros II rules from Debre Tabor (infobox: Debre Tabor 1855-1881).

11 February 1855: Kassa is crowned Tewodros II and the Zemene Mesafint ends. 'its end to Kassa's coronation as Emperor Tewodros II (11 February 1855)'; he 'reunified the Empire' (Ethiopian Empire page).
1881: Yohannes IV rules from Mekelle (infobox: Mekelle 1881-1889).
1881: Ras Gobana Dacche makes Kaffa pay tribute. 'Ras Gobana Dacche forced Kaffa to pay tribute'. The conquest follows (1900 below).

region.text: Jimma, Limmu, Gera and Guma, the Gibe states

ledger.counterpart: Gibe Oromo states (Jimma, Limmu, Gera, Guma)
ledger.note: 1881: Jimma, Limmu, Gera and Guma become tributary. 'Jimma, Limmu, Gera, and Guma became tributary.' They stay tributary; the page gives no later date.
1886: the Arsi submit completely. 'The Arsi temporarily yielded in 1883 and then completely in 1886.'
1886: Gobana Dacche occupies Wollega. 'Gobana Dacche occupied Wollega when Menelik moved his capital to Addis Ababa' in 1886.
1887: Illubabor is incorporated. 'Illubabor was incorporated, pushing the western border back to the Gibe River.' The page's wording is odd; the region is Illubabor.

6 January 1887: Menelik annexes Harar after Chelenqo. 'Harar was annexed to the Kingdom of Shewa', after the Battle of Chelenqo; the Emirate of Harar page: 'finally destroyed and annexed ... in 1887'. Shewa is Menelik's kingdom under Yohannes IV and joins the empire's shape.
1889: the Gurage region is annexed. 'the entire Gurage region was annexed.'
1889: Gobana Dacche annexes Hadiya territory ('Gobana Dacche annexed Hadiya territory').
1889: the capital is Addis Ababa (infobox: Addis Ababa 1889-1974). Menelik was crowned emperor on 3 November 1889 at Entoto; the Menelik II page says he moved his capital to Addis Ababa in 1886.

region.text: the northern edge of the 1769 shape that the 1890 shape no longer holds, the Eritrean highlands

ledger.note: 1890: the northern highlands pass to the Italian colony. The Ethiopian Empire page: 'Italy signed a treaty with Shewa, creating the protectorate of Abyssinia' in 1889; Menelik repudiated it; the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896) 'strictly delineated the borders of Eritrea'. The pages give no date for the cession; the region is the land Cliopatria's shape loses between 1769 and 1890, and Cliopatria's Italian Africa row begins in 1890.

region.text: Bale, Sidamo, the Ogaden and Welayta

ledger.note: 1891: Bale, Sidamo, the Ogaden and Welayta are occupied. 'Bale, Sidamo (excluding Borana), the Ogaden, and Welayta were occupied from 1891 onward.'
1893: the Kambata are fully integrated ('Integration of the Kambata was completed').
1894: Gofa and Wollamo are taken and Mekonnen moves into the Ogaden. 'Welde Giyorgis Aboye moved into Gofa, and Wollamo was conquered.'

region.text: the northern frontier with Eritrea, around Adwa

ledger.note: 1895: war with Italy begins ('1895-1896 (First Italo-Ethiopian War)'). The page names no zone; Tigray is the northern frontier where Adwa lies.

January 1896: Aussa becomes a tributary of the Ethiopian Empire. Welde Giyorgis Aboye 'defeated Sultan Muhammad Hanfare at the battle of Arraddo in January 1896'; 'After this, Aussa became a tributary of the Ethiopian Empire', and Hanfare 'secured a modicum of autonomy within the Ethiopian Empire by accepting Menelik's indirect rule'. The page gives no day or exact treaty; the sultanate keeps its own land (drawn by sultanate-of-aussa).

October 1896: Treaty of Addis Ababa. Menelik 'crushed Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa on 1 March 1896'; the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896) 'strictly delineated the borders of Eritrea' and made Italy recognise Ethiopian independence.
1897: expeditions into Borana ('1896-1897 expeditions were launched into Borana').
1898: Beni Shangul is brought under control and the border with Sudan fixed ('Beni Shangul and the border with Sudan were controlled').
1898: Welde Giyorgis Aboye reaches Lake Rudolf (Turkana).
1898: Ras Tassama annexes Massonge and Gimirra.

1900: Kaffa is completely conquered. The page says Kaffa 'initially resisted' before being 'completely conquered' in the 1896-1900 phase and gives no year; 1900 is the end of that phase (page silent).
1900: Kaffa is annexed (see the vassal_end; the year is a bridge).

region.text: the land Cliopatria adds in 1908, towards Kenya and the western border

ledger.note: 1907: the southern border with British East Africa is first identified. 'first identified by the United Kingdom in 1907'; the Menelik II page: borders were defined 'through treaties with Britain, France, and Italy' (no dates), and Cliopatria enlarges the shape in 1908. The region is that enlargement.

region.text: Adwa, Aksum and Mekelle, taken October-November 1935

ledger.note: 3 October 1935: Italy invades Ethiopia. 'On 3 October 1935, two hundred thousand soldiers of the Regio Esercito' attacked from Eritrea; Adwa fell 6 October, Aksum 15 October and Mekelle 8 November.

1 April 1936: Italy occupies the sultanate. 'On 1 April 1936, the Sultanate was invaded and occupied by the Italians during the Second Italo-Ethiopian War'; Sultan Muhammad Yayyo 'cooperated with the Italian invaders', ending Aussa's tributary status to the Ethiopian Empire before the fall of Addis Ababa on 5 May.

region.text: the empire, overrun by the Italians

ledger.note: 5 May 1936: Addis Ababa falls. 'At 4pm on 5 May, Badoglio drove into the city'; Haile Selassie had left on 2 May. Gondar fell 1 April, Dessie 15 April.

9 May 1936: Italy annexes Ethiopia. Mussolini 'announced the annexation of Ethiopia on 9 May'; on 1 June 1936 the territories were unified as Italian East Africa. Sovereignty returned on 5 May 1941 (Ethiopian Empire page).

wars.name: Amda Seyon's campaigns against Damot, Hadiya, Gojjam and Ifat
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory: Damot, Hadiya and Gojjam conquered 1316, the northern provinces campaigned 1329, Ifat made a vassal 1332 and Ethiopian rule carried across the Awash into Dawaro and Bale.
wars.note: The page warns the chronicles 'appear to be highly unreliable as it was written a century after his reign'; 1329 is Huntingford's date for the Ifat campaign.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal wars of Yeshaq I and Zara Yaqob
wars.outcome: No border change the pages name: Yeshaq I was killed fighting the Adalites in 1429 and Zara Yaqob defeated Sultan Badlay at Gomit in 1445.
wars.note: Adal page infobox: 'War with Yeshaq I: 1415-1429'; Ethiopian Empire page: 'Yeshaq I: killed fighting the Adalites in 1429'.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian-Portuguese victory; status quo ante bellum. Adal held most of the highlands from the mid-1530s; Imam Ahmad was killed at Wayna Daga on 21 February 1543 and Gelawdewos recovered Bali, Fatagar, Dawaro and Hadiya in October 1544.
wars.note: Portuguese musketeers (400 under Cristovao da Gama) landed in February 1541; 700 Ottoman soldiers and ten guns reached Adal in 1542.

wars.name: Oromo expansion into the Ethiopian highlands
wars.outcome: The Oromo overran the empire's southern provinces and tributaries from the 1530s; the page dates Wej 1572, Shewa and Damot 1593, Bale's last tribute 1590-1607, Gojjam and Begemder raids about 1617, and the Wallo and Azebo overrunning Angot and parts of Amhara, Waj, Begemder and Tigre in 1620-1660.
wars.note: Susenyos (1606-1632) and Iyasu I (1682-1706) settled Oromo groups in Gojjam and Begemder as a frontier guard.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Ottoman conflict on the Red Sea coast
wars.outcome: The Ottomans held Massawa and the coast as Habesh Eyalet from 1557; Sarsa Dengel sacked Arqiqo in 1589, containing them on a narrow coastline strip.

wars.name: Funj-Ethiopian wars
wars.outcome: Frontier wars with no border change the page names: a full-fledged war in 1618-1619 and a Funj army on the Dinder River in March 1744.
wars.note: Funj Sultanate page: 'escalated into a full-fledged war in 1618 and 1619'; 'In March 1744 he assembled an army of 30,000-100,000 men'.

wars.name: Zemene Mesafint civil wars
belligerents: Regional lords of Tigray, Yejju, Shewa, Gojjam, Simien and Begemder
wars.outcome: Regional lords (Tigray, Yejju, Shewa, Gojjam, Simien, Begemder) fought for power until Tewodros II's coronation on 11 February 1855 (Battle of Derasge, 1855).
wars.note: No territory changed hands between states; the shape is the nominal realm.

wars.name: British expedition to Abyssinia
wars.outcome: The British expedition succeeded; Tewodros II 'committed suicide rather than surrender'. No border changed.

wars.name: Conquests of Menelik II
wars.outcome: Tribute from Kaffa and the Gibe states (1881); the Arsi (1886), Wollega (1886), Harar (6 January 1887), Illubabor (1887), the Gurage (1889), Bale, Sidamo, the Ogaden and Welayta (from 1891), Kambata (1893), Gofa and Wollamo (1894), Borana (1896-97), Beni Shangul, Lake Rudolf, Massonge and Gimirra (1898) and Kaffa (by 1900).

wars.name: First Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory at Adwa on 1 March 1896; the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896) delineated Eritrea's borders and Italy recognised Ethiopian independence.
wars.note: The Menelik II page repudiates the Wuchale treaty in 1891 (the Ethiopian Empire page says 1893); Wuchale was signed on 2 May 1889.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Mahdist War
wars.outcome: Yohannes IV died in 1889 fighting the Mahdists (Ethiopian Empire page); the page gives no territorial change.
wars.note: Only the death of Yohannes IV is dated on the page.

wars.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Addis Ababa fell on 5 May 1936, annexation 9 May, Italian East Africa formed on 1 June 1936; sovereignty restored 5 May 1941.

certainty.note: Highland provinces, Muslim marches and the southern tributaries have no surveyed frontier; the lines are approximate throughout, and in 1769-1855 the emperor's actual control was Gondar.

The Eritrean frontier was 'strictly delineated' by the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896) and the treaties with Britain, France and Italy 'defined borders' (Menelik II page), but no page dates them; the Ogaden and Kenya frontiers were still unsettled.
The year of the Italian conquest; control was incomplete.

notes:
One state from the Solomonic restoration to the Italian annexation; Cliopatria's single row 1272..1935 is not split because the pages treat it as one empire (Solomonic dynasty, with the Era of the Princes inside). Start moved to 1270 (zagwe-dynasty hands over), end moved to 1936 (annexed 9 May 1936; Cliopatria stops in 1935 and its Italian Africa row draws Ethiopia from 1936).

Cliopatria problems found: (1) the 1547, 1564, 1579 and 1636 shapes (524-587 thousand km2) have no support and contradict the Oromo losses; they are marked adjust with the pre-war 1502 shape (1547-1635) and the 1769 shape (1636-1768) as the page-backed extent. (2) The Ifat row runs to 1414 although the sultanate fell in 1403 (new keyframe 1404). (3) Cliopatria restores the highlands in 1547, not 1543-44. (4) The Eritrean highlands: the 1769 shape includes them throughout; the Zemene Mesafint page says Ethiopian territorial integrity weakened in the north ('Eritrea ... Islamized by the Ottoman Empire and later Eyalet of Egypt') and the Ethiopian Empire page has Yohannes IV re-expanding into Eritrea in 1874-1876 (Gundet); not settled within the page budget. (5) The 1890 cut of the north is dated by no page (ledger 1890 at confidence 1).

Gaps at confidence 1: the 1329 northern campaign as a gain; the Ifat land 1403-1415; the 1890 loss of Eritrea; Kaffa's conquest year (page gives 1896-1900); the 1907 border event; the 1895 start of the Adwa war. Page-budget gaps: the Wuchale treaty and First Italo-Ethiopian War pages (the Eritrean border) and the border treaties 1897-1908 were not opened; the 1900, 1905 and 1908 jumps are kept ok on the Menelik and Kenya-border pages.

Disagreements: Gondar 1635 (infobox) vs 1636 (text); capital moved to Addis Ababa 1886 (Menelik page) vs 1889 (infobox); Wuchale repudiation 1891 (Menelik page) vs 1893 (Ethiopian Empire page); Amda Seyon's Ifat campaign 1332 (accepted) vs 1329 (Huntingford); Wayna Daga is undated on the Adal page (21 February 1543 on the war page).

Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-damot, hadiya-sultanate, emirate-of-harar (1647-1887), kingdom-of-kaffa; the Gibe states (Jimma etc.); the Oromo are not a state ('nobody'). Gazetteer names needed: Damot, Hadiya, Semien, Dawaro, Bale, Fatagar, Wej, Bete Amhara, Kaffa, Arsi, Wollega, Illubabor, Gurage, Sidamo, Welayta, Kambata, Gofa, Wollamo, Borana, Massango, Gimirra. Capitals Debre Tabor and Mekelle coordinates are the researcher's. Rulers omitted: the pages opened give only partial reign years.
